# Valence — Equity Valuation & Financial Modeling Workbench

Valence is a free, browser-based equity-valuation platform and 3-statement financial
modeling workbench for US and Indian equities. It integrates multi-source financial
data ingestion, taxonomy normalization, driver-based 5-year forecasting, WACC estimation
via CAPM, dual terminal-value methodologies, reverse-DCF growth solvers, public trading
comps benchmarking, football-field valuation-range synthesis, PE exit-return waterfalls,
automated accounting QA validation, a 30-tab Excel model exporter with live dynamic
formulas, and a real-time web dashboard.

URL: https://valence.sourabhpradhan.in/
Author: Sourabh (https://sourabh08.vercel.app/)
Source: https://github.com/karbburn

---

## What Valence does

Valence lets an analyst value a public company end-to-end in the browser:

- Search any onboarded US (NASDAQ/NYSE) or Indian (NSE/BSE) ticker.
- Inspect a normalized 3-statement model (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow).
- Override operating drivers and instantly recompute the model.
- Switch between Base, Bull, and Bear scenarios.
- Export a 30-tab Excel model with live formulas.

## Key capabilities

### Driver-based 5-year forecasting
Projects the Income Statement, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow Statement across Base, Bull,
and Bear scenarios, driven by operational metrics: Revenue Growth, EBITDA/EBIT Margins,
CapEx % Revenue, D&A %, DSO, DPO, and Tax Rate.

### Institutional DCF & WACC buildup
Full Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF) build with clean Non-Cash Operating Working Capital
(change in NWC), dynamic WACC estimation (CAPM cost of equity + tax-shielded cost of debt),
Gordon-Growth and Exit EV/EBITDA-Multiple terminal values, and an Enterprise Value to
Implied Share Price bridge.

### Dynamic reverse DCF & 2D sensitivity
Solves for market-implied perpetuity growth rates via exact closed-form inversion, paired
with live 2D sensitivity grids (WACC vs. Terminal Growth, and WACC vs. Exit Multiple).

### Public trading comps & football-field synthesis
Benchmarks the target against sector peers on EV/Sales, EV/EBITDA, P/E, FCF Yield %, and
ROIC %, then synthesizes cross-methodology valuation-range bars (52-week range, DCF
perpetuity, DCF multiple, comps P/E, comps EV/EBITDA, analyst consensus).

### Private-equity exit returns & IRR waterfall
Calculates 3-year and 5-year prospective Exit Equity Value, MoIC (Multiple on Invested
Capital), and Equity IRR (%) under Base, Bull, and Bear exit scenarios, with entry-price
sensitivity grids.

### Multi-market & multi-currency support
Native support for US equities (NASDAQ/NYSE, USD millions) and Indian equities
(NSE/BSE, INR crores), with dynamic currency and unit localization across all statements.

### Automated accounting & model QA engine
Executes nine validation checks: balance-sheet balancing, cash-flow reconciliation, debt
schedule ties, share-count consistency, DCF bridge tie-out, WACC bounds, and data quality.

### 30-tab interactive Excel exporter
Generates 100% dynamic .xlsx workbooks where detail schedules drive the forecast operating
model, featuring live Excel formulas (CAPM, FCFF sums, cross-sheet references, 2D
sensitivity grids, and live =IF(...) audit checks).

## Methodology

### DCF (Discounted Cash Flow)
Valence builds unlevered FCFF and discounts it at the WACC. Two terminal-value methods are
supported: Gordon Growth (perpetuity) and an Exit EV/EBITDA Multiple. Enterprise Value
bridges to Equity Value via net debt, then to an Implied Share Price using diluted shares.

### WACC (CAPM)
Cost of equity is estimated with the Capital Asset Pricing Model; cost of debt is
tax-shielded. Capital weights blend equity and debt at market values.

### Reverse DCF
Given the market price, Valence inverts the DCF to solve for the market-implied perpetuity
growth rate using a closed-form formula.

### Trading comps & football field
Relative valuation benchmarks the target to peers on standard multiples and plots a
football-field range across methods.

### PE returns & IRR
Models a sponsor entry and exit, returning Exit Equity Value, MoIC, and IRR per scenario.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is DCF valuation?** Discounted Cash Flow valuation estimates a company's intrinsic
value by projecting future free cash flows and discounting them to present value at the
weighted average cost of capital (WACC).

**What is WACC?** The Weighted Average Cost of Capital is the blended required return on a
company's equity and debt, used as the discount rate in a DCF.

**Which markets does Valence cover?** US equities (NASDAQ/NYSE, USD) and Indian equities
(NSE/BSE, INR). Coverage is onboarded per ticker.

**Where does the data come from?** SEC EDGAR XBRL (US), Screener.in (India), and live
market feeds, normalized into a unified taxonomy.

**Is Valence free?** Yes. Valence is a free, browser-based workbench.

**Can I export to Excel?** Yes — a 30-tab .xlsx with live, dynamic formulas.

## Author & technology

Valence is built by Sourabh. The core engine is Python 3.12 with Pydantic v2; the web API
is FastAPI + Uvicorn; the Excel renderer uses OpenPyXL and Pillow; data is persisted in
SQLite. The web dashboard is a Next.js application with a custom dark-theme design system.
